units.title: Feedback Loops
units.blurb: Measure, compare, correct: why closing the loop works.

units.title: PID Control
units.blurb: Proportional, integral and derivative, one term at a time.

units.title: Response and Stability
units.blurb: How fast a system settles, and when a controller makes things worse.

topics.title: Open and Closed Loops
topics.short: Open loop runs a fixed command; closed loop measures the error, setpoint minus measurement, and corrects it.
topics.trouble: Students get the sign of the error backward, measurement minus setpoint.

topics.title: Proportional Control
topics.short: Command = Kp times the error, limited to what the motor can give.
topics.trouble: Students forget the motor's limit, so a big error gives an impossible command.

topics.title: One Step of a PID Controller
topics.short: u = Kp e + Ki (sum of e Δt) + Kd (Δe / Δt), computed fresh every loop.
topics.trouble: Students forget Δt in the integral or derivative term, or use the error from the wrong step.

topics.title: Time Constants
topics.short: A first-order system covers 63% of the way to its new value in one time constant τ, and about 99% in 5τ.
topics.trouble: Students think the system arrives after one time constant.

topics.title: Stability and Tuning
topics.short: Too much gain overshoots and can oscillate or diverge; tune P first, then D, then a little I.
topics.trouble: Students keep raising the gain to go faster and are surprised when the robot starts to shake.
